reviews.title: Great App, too pushy with sales
reviews.text:
I like the app as a companion to my tabletop games. I use books, pen & paper, and physical dice.

I can’t access content in the app from a book that I purchased new, so I can’t use the app to track my character’s abilities and resources accurately.

It’s great for referencing rules & spells, but as my campaigns level up, it gets less useful if I don’t spend money.

I wouldn’t mind so much if I had the ability to use material from books I bought, but I don’t want to pay for things twice.

I’m using it less now: just looking spells & conditions I need to reference online, and I don’t miss it much.

reviews.title: Poor accessibility for the Blind
reviews.text: This app is incredibly clunky and difficult to use with VoiceOver on the iPhone. Some things are labelled, some things  are accessible, but overall it is very poor quality. Some of the boxes and windows overlap one another, making it difficult to understand which screen you’re on, and general reaction times from moving around the app is incredibly sluggish. I cannot even create a character using this app. Instead I have to use a combination of three different apps for my character sheet, spells and dice rolls. This hasn’t changed over the years, and it continues to be incredibly poor quality. It is clear the developers don’t want visually impaired people to use this app to play the game.

It’s ok. Handy to have. I don’t think I’ll ever agree with the money grab that says that if you buy physical copies you then have to pay again for digital versions. Whatever way you look at it, that’s just a rip off. 
My major gripe is that if you’re relying on Beyond don’t. Our players all sat at the table, ready to go to find that no one could access their characters or campaign as Beyond was down for maintenance for the whole day. Beyond ridiculous.

reviews.title: Money grab
reviews.text:
The inability to use the app, but also use the hard copies without paying extra for the digital is a rip off. The bundle of the 2 isn’t a great deal, but if you’re going to use DnD beyond it’s about all you can do. Otherwise it’s not even worth using. Constantly being locked out of some of the smallest descriptions and stats for things behind the pay wall is extremely frustrating. Especially since you can literally look up anything elsewhere. They are just banking on everyone being frustrated switching between Google, hard copies, and DnD beyond and it makes the game come to a crawl when you’re just trying to answer simple questions.
It has so much potential, but they want that money so bad. Then they just overload the library with junk that isn’t even official rules.

reviews.title: I can’t sign in
reviews.text:
I just made an account so that me and my friends could set up our first d&d campaign. I wanted to access my account on my iPad rather than on my phone because the screen is bigger, but whenever I try signing in on my iPad I am stuck on the “Updating Sources” page. 

However, if I sign in on my phone it works perfectly fine. My phone is a Samsung, so I think it could be an Apple issue not allowing me to sign in on my iPad rather than an issue with my account. I have been stuck in the same screen for half an hour. I have tried uninstalling and reinstalling the app 3 times, but it still refuses to pass me through the “Updating Sources” page.

reviews.title: Convenient, but not worth it.
reviews.text: I have to give credit where credit is due, this app is no doubt very helpful and convenient. I could totally see why someone would like it, and if you do, good for you. But I honestly think it’s mind boggling that you would expect me to fork over $30 in exchange for some spells and a few races, maybe sprinkle on a weapon. Listen, if you’ve got this, then you’ve got a browser, which means you can literally just look up the race you want to play, or the monster you want to add to your game, or the weapon you want to use. The point is, why should I pay for pretty much everything, when I could just simply look it up for free. Now I acknowledge the counter argument of “but you’d still need to pay for the books, and you can’t get things that aren’t official.” That may be true…..but if you’ve want to use all that stuff….home brew it. For free.
